points.treatment: Ice melting, water warming, rosebud opening and browning banana; distinguish observations from classifications.
All ten named changes and one learner-chosen change retained; source observation blanks replaced by notebook recording. Safe sensory observation replaces unrestricted tasting/touching.
Fold/unfold paper, inflate/deflate/puncture balloon, crush chalk; original material versus original object. Adult pin handling and contained chalk dust.
No new substance; shape, size and state. Water states preserved; visible mist distinguished from vapour.
Tap water and lime-water comparison with exhaled air. Teacher collects and delivers air without mouth-to-liquid connection; untouched controls and uncertain results added.
Calcium hydroxide, carbon dioxide, insoluble calcium carbonate and water; word equation and lime-water test. Excess-gas limitation added.
Vinegar or lemon juice plus baking soda, fizz, gas test and water comparison; test-tube/bottle alternatives. Open outlet and backflow prevention.
Rusting is a chemical change; hydrated iron oxides rather than an oversimplified single dry oxide.
Magnesium oxide, heat/light, combustible wood/paper/cotton/kerosene. Energy distinguished from material products; recall only, no student burning.
Two candles, one covered; air supply versus carbon dioxide product test. Does not claim zero oxygen or that testing CO2 identifies oxygen.
Smothering and no synthetic cloth retained; stop/drop/roll and adult help added.
Bioluminescence with very little heat rather than literally no heat.
Match versus focused sunlight, ignition temperature and three requirements. Teacher-only or video, cleared area, heatproof tray, extinguishing, lens/eye precautions.
All four student observations: melting/evaporating, burning/new substances, wick transport, flowing/resolidifying. Physical and chemical changes together.
Chemical History of a Candle and inquiry through familiar objects; 1861 publication verified.
Return to Table 5.1; source ice/vegetables/boiling/popcorn records and uncertainty preserved with explicit recovery conditions.
Curd, ripe/cut fruit, cooked food, rust, spoilage and compost; purpose determines desirability.
Fuel consumption/CO2 and substances released during paint drying; qualified to fossil fuels and some paints.
Sediments below cliffs, temperature, roots, freezing water, chemical mineral change and red iron-bearing basalt; soil formation.
Wind/water/gravity, landslide, abrasion, settling and sedimentary rocks. Distinguishes change in place from transport; long durations versus rapid events.

corrections.change: Replace blowing directly through a straw into lime water with teacher-collected air and needle-free gas delivery; keep the same comparison.
A flame can go out before oxygen is exhausted; CO2 testing establishes a product, not which air component supports burning.
Warm-iron adult method retained; paper-over-flame alternative removed to avoid an unnecessary fire task.
Yeast/no-yeast control added; teacher tubing transfers collected gas instead of learners shaking lime water with a balloon attached.
Colour has several functions, including communication and temperature response; avoid universal deliberate camouflage claim.
Candle statement asks whether melting helps supply fuel, rather than an absolute necessary-condition claim about every moment of ignition.
Growing plants and ripening organisms may involve several processes; permit justified mixed-process classifications. Gathering objects alone does not establish reaction.
Irreversibility is not the definition of chemical change.
